newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Malawi wheat stranded in Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: Malawi wheat stranded in Mozambique.

text.p: More than 8,000 tonnes of wheat destined for Malawi had been in storage at Mozambique's Nacala port since October because Malawi's wheat market was saturated, the Mozambique News Agency said on Tuesday.
Landlocked Malawi uses Nacala and neighbouring Mozambique's northern rail system to export tobacco and to import fuel, chemicals and grain.
Port director Agostinho Langa told the agency the wheat had arrived from abroad in two consignments -- 3,191 tonnes in July, and 4,815 tonnes in October.
He said the wheat belonged to a private milling company in Malawi which decided to store it after it found Malawi's market had been been flooded with cheap wheat from South Africa.
The company believed storing the wheat at Nacala was cheaper than moving it to Malawi where there were no guarantees of a market, Langa said.
The agency said port authorities were worried because storage space at Nacala was already restricted after a cyclone damaged warehouses in March 1993.
